item.title: Looking forward to Asia-Pacific cooperation soaring high and far on a boundless journey: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 01:41:00
This photo taken on November 16, 2026 shows a view of Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province with APEC elements. China will hold the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19. Photo: VCG The historic gathering of APEC members in Shenzhen will become a new starting point for their joint efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community. From here, the vision of Asia-Pacific cooperation will take flight, transforming the collective strength forged within the conference halls into sustained momentum for regional cooperation in the years ahead. "China is an advocate, promoter and forerunner of Asia-Pacific economic cooperation. We would like to work with all parties to pool wisdom and synergy in building the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community." Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday chaired the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, and delivered important remarks titled "Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle." Focusing on new opportunities and challenges facing the Asia-Pacific region and the world, the Chinese leader, for the first time in the history of APEC, systematically expounded China's proposition on what kind of Asia-Pacific community to build and how to build it, and reaffirmed China's steadfast commitment to supporting Asia-Pacific cooperation, while demonstrating a great sense of responsibility and a global vision in leading and promoting cooperation both within the Asia-Pacific and across the globe. More than three decades ago, APEC was born as the times required, embarking on a grand journey toward building an Asia-Pacific community. Over the past 30-plus years, the Asia-Pacific region has undergone profound transformations, creating an "Asia-Pacific miracle" of rapid economic growth. Today, the region has become an anchor of stability for global development. Whether the Asia-Pacific can continue to write this success story concerns not only the general well-being of the economies within the region but also the broader landscape of world peace and development. Faced with this pressing question of the times, the leaders and representatives of 21 economies convened in Shenzhen to chart the course for the future of Asia-Pacific cooperation. This marks the first time in recent years that a full "family photo" of APEC members has been realized, a clear testament to the shared aspiration of all parties for mutually beneficial cooperation. The Chinese side proposed that, in the face of new opportunities and challenges, Asia-Pacific cooperation must adapt to the new realities, take new strides, and open up new prospects and strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development. As an advocate, promoter and forerunner of Asia-Pacific economic cooperation, China is willing to work with all parties to pool wisdom and synergy in strengthening the pillar of economy and trade, upgrading the pillar of connectivity, fostering the pillar of innovation and enhancing the pillar of development. The economy and trade pillar serves as the bedrock and the essential foundation for Asia-Pacific cooperation. The connectivity pillar is a vital support, having effectively underpinned nearly half of the region's cooperative endeavors over the past 12 years. The innovation pillar serves as the primary engine for growth, driving the digital, intelligent, and green transformation of the Asia-Pacific region. The development pillar embodies a people-centered value orientation and offers the key to resolving complex challenges inherent in globalization and regional economic integration. These four pillars complement and reinforce one another, collectively supporting the edifice of an Asia-Pacific community. The Asia-Pacific is where China has its roots and where its future lies. To support Asia-Pacific cooperation, China has introduced a series of concrete supporting measures: providing funding to support APEC practical cooperation, establishing a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies, and setting up cooperation institutions in areas such as digital technology, cross-border data flows, clean energy, and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises. These initiatives impose no exclusionary barriers. Instead, they focus on building platforms, establishing mechanisms, and promoting shared benefits, ensuring that the outcomes of cooperation are visible, tangible, and accessible. China will continue to honor its commitments through concrete actions, working with all parties to ensure that cooperation projects take root and bear fruit. It will inject fresh momentum into the building of an Asia-Pacific community and provide tangible support for the "four pillars" through the provision of more practical public goods. The meeting unanimously adopted the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which put forward the "Shenzhen Vision" for building an Asia-Pacific community, along with three outcome documents covering trade, connectivity, and innovation. As the most significant outcome of the APEC "China Year" and a new milestone in APEC cooperation, the "Shenzhen Vision" reaffirms APEC's role as the primary platform for regional economic cooperation. Guided by the principles of voluntary participation, non-binding arrangements, and consensus-building, it commits to transforming APEC into a more modern, efficient, and pragmatic incubator of ideas. The tides of Shenzhen Bay bear witness to the powerful momentum of Asia-Pacific cooperation. APEC members are transforming their shared commitment to standing together through challenges into tangible connections spanning mountains and oceans. From the Port of Chancay opening new routes for Asia-Pacific supply chains and the Pinglu Canal strengthening land-sea links between southwestern China and Southeast Asia, to Juncao technology taking root in Pacific Island countries; from the Asia-Pacific Model E-Port Network significantly improving the efficiency of cross-border customs clearance and cross-border electricity transmission lines linking the region's clean energy resources, to APEC cooperation zones for small and medium-sized enterprises building bridges that connect countless small and micro businesses to shared markets, these concrete projects are weaving a strong connection. Through practical cooperation, the contours of an Asia-Pacific community are becoming ever clearer and more tangible. Over the past 30-plus years, China and the Asia-Pacific have advanced together, reinforcing each other's development and achieving shared prosperity through openness. Today, as a new chapter begins, China's high-standard opening-up and high-quality development will bring fresh development opportunities to the Asia-Pacific. The historic gathering of APEC members in Shenzhen will become a new starting point for their joint efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community. From here, the vision of Asia-Pacific cooperation will take flight, transforming the collective strength forged within the conference halls into sustained momentum for regional cooperation in the years ahead. Amid a rapidly changing global landscape, this momentum will provide a firm foundation for an Asia-Pacific home that belongs to all its members and is defined by shared prosperity.

item.title: China-Russia-US summit is unprecedented and makes history: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 01:35:00
Photo: Xinhua China, Russia and the US have different national conditions, but this doesn't mean confrontation is inevitable. By communicating in advance, considering issues from one another's perspectives and acting with caution on major sensitive matters involving each other's interests, particularly by refraining from crossing each other's red lines, major powers can indeed avoid the "Thucydides Trap." Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday afternoon held a China-Russia-US summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province. President Xi made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace: Major countries should uphold mutual respect, uphold peaceful coexistence, uphold win-win cooperation, and uphold dialogue and consultation. The four "upholds" outline a clear path and set of rules for building a new model of major-country relations, and provide important guidance for China, Russia, and the US to strengthen strategic communication and practical cooperation and jointly safeguard world peace. The core agenda of this summit centers on two key dimensions: safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-country relations. These issues not only determine the future trajectory of major-country relations but are also inextricably linked to the vital development interests of nations across the globe. Looking back at the evolution of the international order, humanity has taken many wrong turns in the management of major-country relations. Since modern times, the rise of many emerging powers has been accompanied by intense geopolitical conflicts; the harrowing lessons of the two world wars, for instance, were rooted in zero-sum games played by major powers. Peace among major countries brings stability to the world, while their contention would only lead to chaos. Forging a new, right path for major countries to get along serves the interests of the three nations and aligns with the expectations of the international community. Can major countries move beyond the narrative of competition and achieve constructive interactions? This is a question that China, Russia and the US must answer. Historically, as the principal victors of the anti-fascist alliance in World War II, the three countries fought side by side to defeat militarism and fascism, laying the foundations for the postwar international order underpinned by the United Nations Charter. Firmly upholding the postwar international order, safeguarding the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and defending the hard-won achievements of victory in World War II are both a historical responsibility shared by the three countries as victors and a common commitment to all peace-loving nations around the world. As major countries of the world and permanent members of the UN Security Council, China, Russia and the US should, and can, set an example by working together to address global challenges, jointly safeguarding world peace and stability. In today's world, the overarching trends of economic globalization and global multipolarity are irreversible, but they are also facing enormous challenges. Against the backdrop of frequent fluctuations in international energy prices and an uneven transition from traditional energy to new-energy sources, the international community is deeply concerned about energy security, the security of shipping routes, and the security of industrial and supply chains. Enhanced communication and coordination among China, Russia, and the US will help prevent major countries from falling into vicious competition over resources, technology, and corridors, help maintain the stability and smooth functioning of energy industrial and supply chains, and help safeguard the stability of the global energy market. China, Russia and the US have different national conditions, but this doesn't mean confrontation is inevitable. By communicating in advance, considering issues from one another's perspectives and acting with caution on major sensitive matters involving each other's interests, particularly by refraining from crossing each other's red lines, major powers can indeed avoid the "Thucydides Trap." The Taiwan question lies at the very core of China's core interests and constitutes the first red line that must not be crossed by any country seeking to develop relations with China. For a long time, the reason "Taiwan independence" separatist forces have repeatedly dared to test the limits of danger is precisely that they have clung to the illusion of exploiting tensions among major countries, attempting to profit from their rivalries. The leaders of China, Russia and the US share common views on safeguarding world peace and have reached a series of important consensuses on maintaining strategic stability and international security. This means that the space in which "Taiwan independence" forces have imagined they could survive by exploiting divisions among major countries is steadily narrowing. Many analysts believe that without China's sustained efforts and its role as the host, this "historic gathering" would probably have been difficult to achieve. While we will not engage in hypothetical analysis, it is undeniable that China played an important role in facilitating the meeting. This is closely linked to China's position as a responsible major country and its diplomatic philosophy of promoting a new model of major-country relations. Both the Russian and US leaders expressed appreciation to China for hosting this historic meeting. The meeting represents not only an important milestone in the history of international relations, but also a landmark event in major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics. The China-Russia-US Heads of State Declaration toward Peace released after the summit represents a joint solution of peace provided by the three countries based on both current and future situations. Its provisions on reforming the United Nations, reaffirming the importance of stable energy flows, and emphasizing that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought largely echo the four points made by the Chinese side on how major countries should get along with each other. Certainly, a single meeting cannot resolve every problem. But as long as countries uphold mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, mutually beneficial cooperation, and dialogue and consultation, a way forward can always be found. The China-Russia-US summit in Shenzhen can be seen as a starting point, opening up new possibilities for constructive interactions among major countries and for exploring the right way for them to get along. It also represents an important attempt by major countries to jointly explore constructing a new type of major-country relations in an era of multipolarity. The seeds sown by the meeting of the three heads of state will surely take root, sprout, bloom, and bear fruit.

item.title: China, Russia, US hold groundbreaking summit in South China's Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 00:17:00
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Photo: Xinhua) Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday afternoon held a China-Russia-US summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, stressing that the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the Chinese, Russian and US heads of state is of groundbreaking significance. While summarizing the main consensus reached at the summit, Xi said that the China-Russia-US summit has been positive, constructive and fruitful. The three countries share the same view on safeguarding world peace, and all stressed that the hard-won peace must be cherished, Xi said. Following the summit, the China-Russia-US Heads of State Declaration toward Peace was released, which stated that the Russian and US heads of state expressed appreciation to China for hosting this historic trilateral Summit, and the three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security. The historic summit among leaders of three permanent members of the United Nations Security Council drew widespread international attention, as it charts a new course of major-power relations by strengthening dialogue and coordination so as to reduce misunderstanding and risks, which injects a much-needed sense of stability for the world, experts noted. Chinese President Xi Jinping speaks with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump before a welcome banquet in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province on November 18, 2026. Photo: People's Daily Historic summit The Chinese President made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace. Major countries should uphold mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation, Xi said at the summit. The Chinese leader said that countries should respect one another's sovereignty and territorial integrity, respect the social systems and development paths of their own choice, and respect each other's core interests and major concerns. They should not interfere in other countries' domestic affairs or each other's internal affairs, he said. On major sensitive issues concerning one another, it is important to communicate in advance, try to see things from the others' perspective, act with caution, and in particular, not to challenge one another's red lines, Xi said. The Chinese President said that China, Russia and the US should be partners and friends. They should not go for conflict or confrontation among themselves, but should hold the line on peaceful coexistence and make efforts to avoid the Thucydides Trap. As the main victors of World War II, China, Russia and the United States should steadfastly safeguard the postwar international order, the Chinese leader said. The summit lasted approximately one and a half hours, according to media reports. The Kremlin has released a video showing Putin leaving the summit venue and saying goodbye to Xi. "Thank you for organizing this," Putin said. Commenting on the trilateral meeting, Trump said that "I'm delighted that this trip has also given us the opportunity for this first ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China," per AP. "So in that sense, and I think in lots of other ways, we are really making history," he added. At a time when competition and confrontation have come to define relations among major countries, the historic trilateral summit could help ease tensions, improve coordination and bring greater stability to their interactions, Cui Hongjian, a professor at the Academy of Regional and Global Governance at Beijing Foreign Studies University, told the Global Times. Cui said the summit could encourage the three countries to find common ground and make compromises, arguing that more stable relations among them would be essential to addressing some of the world's most pressing challenges. The statement underscored China's longstanding commitment to building a new model of relations among major powers. "History reflects the experiences of certain countries, but those experiences do not necessarily dictate how major powers must interact with one another," he said. The trilateral summit underscored China's growing role in managing relations among major powers, Yang Xiyu, a senior research fellow at the China Institute of International Studies, told the Global Times. Yang said Beijing had maintained close diplomatic engagement with both Moscow and Washington throughout the year, helping lay the groundwork for the historic meeting. China is not only playing an active role in shaping the international order but is also helping create opportunities for dialogue among major powers with competing strategic interests, bringing countries with deep-seated differences to the negotiating table. Such efforts could strengthen Beijing's influence in global affairs while demonstrating its willingness to look beyond its own national interests and take on greater responsibility for international peace and stability, he added. Stabilizer for world peace Following the summit, the three countries issued China-Russia-US Heads of State Declaration toward Peace. As permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, China, Russia, and the United States committed to reform the UN so that the UN can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security, according to the declaration. The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows, it reads. The three heads of state recognized that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction, according to the declaration. Moreover, it states that the three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. The declaration addressed some of the world's most pressing challenges, including energy security and nuclear arms control, areas in which the three countries not only share common interests but also have significant differences, Li Yonghui, a researcher at the Institute of Russian, East European and Central Asian Studies at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, told the Global Times. Li said the declaration underscored that while competition and disagreements among major powers are inevitable, they should not undermine the international order, much less push the world toward war. "Maintaining peace, respecting national sovereignty, promoting economic cooperation and sharing responsibility for global security should be the fundamental principles guiding international relations," Li said. Far-reaching effect During the summit, the Chinese President also said that nuclear weapons, the Sword of Damocles that hangs over humanity, should be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time to make the world free of nuclear weapons. Cui said nuclear arms control was an essential topic for the trilateral summit, as ongoing conflicts in several parts of the world have renewed fears about the risks posed by weakening nuclear safeguards. Against this backdrop, China is seeking to encourage the US and Russia to strengthen arms control efforts, he said. The trilateral meeting has also had a ripple effect on other countries. Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto expressed hope for constructive outcomes from the summit. "I would like at this moment also to express our admiration and our hopes for the historic meeting that is taking place at this APEC Summit between the three leaders of the three great powers of the world," Prabowo said, according to Indonesia news agency Antara. Yang said that bringing the three major powers together to strengthen dialogue, prevent misunderstandings and manage differences would not only contribute to global peace and stability but could also encourage other countries to take on greater international responsibilities. Zhang Ruiqi also contributed to the story

item.title: China-based scientist wins APS's highest award in measurement science
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20 00:00:00
Pan Shuheng (center) with key members of his research team. Photo: Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences Pan Shuheng, a researcher at the Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), was named a recipient of the American Physical Society's 2027 Joseph F. Keithley Award for Advances in Measurement Science in recognition of his pioneering invention of the Pan-type scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) scan head, as well as his foundational research and development work in low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy, the institute announced on Thursday. Pan is the first researcher based in China to receive the award, according to the Science and Technology Daily. Pan has long been engaged in cutting-edge condensed matter physics research, with extensive expertise in scanning tunneling microscopy, the Science and Technology Daily reported. His work has transformed the scanning tunneling microscope from a tool primarily used to observe nanoscale surface morphology into a platform capable of quantitative spectroscopic analysis and imaging. It has supported a range of groundbreaking precision-measurement research in condensed matter physics and significantly expanded the ability to observe and characterize microscopic states of matter under extreme conditions, the Science and Technology Daily reported, citing the institute. Established in 1997, the Joseph F. Keithley Award for Advances in Measurement Science is a prestigious international award in the fields of precision measurement and instrumentation science and is the American Physical Society's highest honor in the field of measurement science. Since 1998, the award has been presented annually to researchers worldwide, the Science and Technology Daily reported. Since the award was established, its recipients have predominantly come from leading research institutions in Europe and the US. Global Times

item.title: Chinese universities expand English course exemptions to recognize students' language proficiency
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 23:51:00
The campus of Shenzhen University in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, on May 16, 2026. Photo: VCG Several Chinese universities are reforming English teaching by allowing students to earn course credits through language test scores and competition results, offering more flexible study options while retaining proficiency requirements. The changes have drawn public attention, with experts saying they can spare students repetitive coursework and make teaching better suited to different learning needs. An academic affairs staff member at Jiangnan University in Wuxi, East China's Jiangsu Province, told Jiupai News on Wednesday that students could apply for exemptions using scores from the College English Test Band 4 and Band 6, known as CET-4 and CET-6, as well as IELTS and TOEFL. Students who do not meet the exemption criteria must still attend classes, the staff member said. The clarification followed reports that the university had made college English courses elective. Other universities introducing similar arrangements include Guangzhou University and Shenzhen University in South China's Guangdong Province and the University of Shanghai for Science and Technology. Rules published on September 20 by the official WeChat account of Jiangnan University's School of Foreign Studies set out several routes to exemptions. Alongside CET, IELTS, and TOEFL scores, students can submit results from tests of intercultural competence and international communication, or awards from English competitions. Exemptions apply to courses in specified semesters, with course grade points determined by the results submitted. Under the rules, eligible students with an IELTS score of 7.5 or above can be exempted from college English in their third and fourth semesters and receive the maximum grade of 4.0 for each course. The University of Shanghai for Science and Technology and Shenzhen University also issued notices in September allowing qualifying language scores to count as college English course grades. The Shanghai university lists seven English courses covered by its arrangements, including college English, academic English reading and writing, and academic English listening and speaking. Its policy extends to other foreign languages. Students can use Japanese-Language Proficiency Test N1 results or J.TEST A-C test results for Japanese course recognition, while German qualifications include the Goethe-Zertifikat, TestDaF, and the German Language Diploma, or DSD. An N1 score of at least 170 can be recognized as a Japanese course mark of 95, while a Goethe-Zertifikat C1 qualification can be recognized as a German course mark of 95. The changes have won support on social media but also prompted concerns that universities are reducing the importance of English, according to Chinese media reports. The universities have made clear that exemptions are based on students' actual language proficiency, Xiong Bingqi, director of the 21st Century Education Research Institute, told the Global Times on Thursday. Students who have demonstrated the required proficiency through CET-4, CET-6, IELTS, or TOEFL should not have to repeat courses covering material they have already mastered, Xiong said. Recognizing that ability through exemptions and credits allows them to devote more time to subjects that interest them and areas of their major requiring deeper study. The standards remain in place, he stressed. Students whose results fall below the required thresholds must still take English classes, complete assessments, and earn the necessary credits. Such exemptions allow teaching to accommodate different starting points through flexible, competence-based arrangements, he said. Those differences can emerge well before students enter university. Some have already developed strong English skills in middle or high school, making instruction tailored to different proficiency levels necessary, Ding Changfa, an associate professor in the Department of Economics at Xiamen University, was quoted by Chinese media outlet Yicai as saying. Ding also pointed to the impact of artificial intelligence on how languages are used and learned, saying university English teaching needs to adapt to these changes. As universities seek to train people with skills spanning different disciplines, their teaching should evolve accordingly, Ding said. For English courses, differentiated instruction can help shift the emphasis from language knowledge toward the ability to use English in professional settings, bringing learning closer to the needs of economic and social development.

item.title: Northern China rolls out 'snow breaks' to turn winter activities into learning opportunities beyond classroom
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 23:10:00
Snow covers the partially frozen Songhua River in Harbin, Northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, on November 18, 2026. Photo: VCG As autumn breaks continue to make headlines, several northern Chinese regions are introducing another seasonal school holiday: the snow break. Students in Zhangjiakou, North China's Hebei Province, began their first snow break on Wednesday, while Jilin Province, Hulunbuir in North China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, and Altay in Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region have also announced their 2026 arrangements. The initiative seeks to make use of local ice and snow resources, turning winter activities into opportunities for learning beyond the classroom. Jiang Yiyi, dean of the School of Leisure Sports and Tourism at Beijing Sport University, told the Global Times on Thursday that the snow break represents a positive exploration of local education governance, moving away from a uniform school calendar toward arrangements tailored to regional conditions and seasonal characteristics. Unlike traditional winter and summer vacations, which mainly follow academic schedules and climatic conditions, the snow break directly turns the distinctive ice and snow resources of northern China into educational resources, Jiang said. "It allows the holiday to become an extension of school-based courses and social practice, rather than simply a pause in classroom learning." The initiative also carries broader significance, Jiang said. It offers opportunities to integrate physical education, aesthetic education, and labor education into real-life experiences, supports the development of winter sports among young people, and creates potential synergies between education and local tourism. Local arrangements reflect these goals. Jilin plans to offer students free skiing and skating experiences, as well as access to selected tourist attractions and public cultural and sports venues. Hulunbuir is incorporating activities such as dryland curling and floorball, while Altay is encouraging students to take part in winter-themed study tours, folk culture activities, and science education programs. The growing popularity of winter sports provides a broader context for the initiatives. According to data released by the Winter Sports Administrative Center of China's General Administration of Sport, 308 million people participated in ice and snow sports nationwide during the 2025-26 winter season, including nearly 69 million children and teenagers. However, turning a seasonal holiday into a meaningful educational experience requires more than simply issuing a vacation notice. Jiang highlighted three major challenges: childcare provision, activity safety, and equitable access to resources. For families with both parents working, a school holiday can create additional childcare pressure. Without adequate support, the burden may fall disproportionately on families with limited caregiving options. Local authorities and schools should provide a combination of on-campus childcare, community-based services, and public winter camps throughout the holiday, Jiang said. Safety is another concern. Jiang noted that skiing and skating require professional instruction, suitable equipment, and proper supervision. School-organized activities should have clear standards for instructors, venues, student-to-teacher ratios, insurance, and emergency response plans. Public safety training and venue certification can also help families make informed choices when arranging activities independently. Unequal access to facilities and services could further widen existing gaps between urban and rural students. If snow-break activities rely mainly on commercial ski resorts and paid courses, the holiday could become an opportunity available only to families who can afford it. The success of a special holiday should not be measured by how many days students are given off, but by whether they return healthier, more confident, and more familiar with their hometowns, while their parents can enjoy peace of mind, Jiang added.

item.title: Xi charts new blueprint for Asia-Pacific development at APEC meeting in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 22:42:00
Chinese President Xi Jinping poses for a group photo with leaders and representatives from other economies before the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. Xi chaired the meeting and delivered important remarks titled "Building an Asia-Pacific Community and Writing a New Chapter of the Asia-Pacific Miracle" on Thursday. (Photo: Xinhua) Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the "Asia-Pacific miracle" in a speech as he chaired the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, charting a clear blueprint for Asia-Pacific development over the next decade and beyond at a time when regional cooperation stands at a historic crossroads. The speech, which outlined the "four key pillars" of an Asia-Pacific community, alongside concrete Chinese pledges, represents a systematic Chinese approach to addressing the defining questions of our time - how to sustain cooperation amid differences, preserve openness amid competition, and unlock new growth drivers amid technological transformation, APEC officials, business leaders and experts said. Amid mounting pressures from rising protectionism, geopolitical uncertainties, and rapid industrial shifts, the speech offers a structured framework for cooperation upon which the "Asia-Pacific miracle" over three decades and more can march into a new chapter, analysts said. The meeting adopted by consensus the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which sets out the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, and three outcome documents on trade, connectivity and innovation. The Shenzhen Outlook, which not only consolidates political consensus among the 21 member economies, but also sends a clear signal of accelerating the translation of grand visions into concrete implementation. Observers said the Shenzhen Outlook carries great significance, as how Asia-Pacific economies navigate headwinds and forge shared interests through pragmatic cooperation will not only shape the trajectory of regional development, but also offer valuable practical experience for global economic governance amid turbulence and transformation. Four pillars "Together, we must strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development," Xi said. China is an advocate, promoter and forerunner of Asia-Pacific economic cooperation. We would like to work with all parties to pool wisdom and synergy in building the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community, the Chinese president noted. He suggested that we should strengthen the pillar of economy and trade, upgrade the pillar of connectivity, foster the pillar of innovation and enhance the pillar of development. Many of the points touched on in the speech drew widespread resonance across the board. For example, some foreign attendees said that the proposal of "four key pillars" directly addresses the core needs of the Asia-Pacific business community, demonstrating China's global vision linking its own development with shared regional prosperity. In 2014, when China hosted the APEC in Beijing, "the emphasis was on building a more connected Asia-Pacific. In 2026, the challenge is how to preserve that connectivity, strengthen its resilience and ensure that its benefits are more widely shared, and this is where I see continuity in China's approach," Antonio I. Basilio, Director of the APEC Business Advisory Council Secretariat, told the Global Times. From a corporate perspective, Saravoot Yoovidhya, CEO of Thailand's TCP Group, told the Global Times on Thursday that the blueprint across the four pillars of trade, connectivity, innovation, and development closely aligns with the operations and long-term growth of the business community across APEC. "This top-level design not only strengthens corporate confidence in long-term regional investment, but also delivers tangible operational convenience, opens up new space for industrial upgrading, and builds a broad stage for multi-party collaboration," he said, expressing hope for deeper China-ASEAN industrial synergy across digital and green transformation, supply chain cooperation, and people-to-people exchanges in the future. When discussing smoother trade flows among APEC economies, Sean Stein, President of the US-China Business Council, cited the Chinese idiom "houji bofa" — meaning steady accumulation leading to long-term gains. "Every year of APEC builds on that, and over time, that makes everyone more prosperous, and everyone's economy better," he told the Global Times, adding that China can do a great deal to make trade, investment, and commerce across all APEC economies "more efficient." On the pillars of innovation and development, business leaders and scholars pointed to frontier technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and the green transition as the Asia-Pacific region's next major growth engines. "With the world's densest manufacturing base, richest application scenarios, and most complete supply networks, the Asia-Pacific is a natural testing ground for AI to move from the digital realm into the physical world, reshaping how products are made and supply chains operate," Zhou Xing, Vice Chair of PwC China, told the Global Times on Thursday. Meanwhile, the Asia-Pacific is both the world's major energy consumption center and stands at the forefront of the energy transition. So the vision of building an Asia-Pacific community points to concrete avenues for regional energy cooperation, including cross-border energy storage and hydrogen initiatives, Zhou noted. "Every step forward in aligning rules opens up new room for growth," she said. From proposals to actions "China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation. I hereby announce that China will provide $20 million to support APEC's practical cooperation," Xi said in the speech. "Rather than remaining at the conceptual level, the Chinese approach focused on concrete implementation across customs, cross-border payments, and supply chain stability," Wang Yuzhu, a distinguished professor at Shenzhen University and vice president of the Chinese Association of Asia-Pacific Studies, told the Global Times on Thursday. Meanwhile, the 2026 APEC Leaders' Shenzhen Outlook adopted on Thursday charts a pragmatic roadmap across four core areas: trade and investment, connectivity, innovation, and economic growth. The document reaffirms APEC's commitment to advancing market-driven regional integration, including through the FTAAP agenda. APEC economic leaders also endorsed several initiatives, including the APEC Connectivity Blueprint and the APEC Statement on Harnessing Digital and Emerging Technologies for Employment and Prosperity, while welcoming the APEC Trade Digitalization Cooperation Framework (2027-2030) and commending the APEC AI Initiative (2026-2030). Wang said the Shenzhen Outlook aims to ensure freer flows of goods, capital, and people across the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP) - an initiative China proposed at the APEC meeting in 2014, while harnessing the digital economy, AI, and industrial innovation as open growth engines rather than making frontier technology behind closed doors. This will enable economies of all sizes - whether developing or developed - to share the dividends of growth across areas, Wang said. Standing at the new starting point of the Shenzhen APEC meeting, looking back on more than three decades of the "Asia-Pacific miracle" makes the region's upcoming new decade more exciting - a juncture where China's own development blueprint is deeply converging with the future of the Asia-Pacific. The "Asia-Pacific miracle" of the past three decades was built on open trade, investment, and cross-border industrial division of labor. As these foundations face mounting external pressures today, China's proposals offer not only a long-term vision for an Asia-Pacific community, but also a systematic cooperation framework to sustain that miracle, analysts said. They also pointed out that China's vast market, complete manufacturing system, and practical experience in digital technology, clean energy, and infrastructure provide tangible opportunities for regional cooperation. In this context, the proposals reflect China's strategic vision of linking its own development opportunities with regional growth, while helping shape a more open, interconnected, and inclusive Asia-Pacific economic environment through actionable agendas and concrete strengths. That convergence is set to deepen as 2026 marks the opening year of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30), further turning the country's next five-year blueprint into a shared engine of regional growth. Speaking on inclusive development, Alastair Symington, CEO of Australia's Blackmores, told the Global Times that as China embarks on its 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30), the clear signal from Shenzhen shows that China is stepping up to shoulder more responsibility and leadership within the Asia-Pacific community. With regard to China's role in APEC, former Singaporean foreign minister George Yeo told the Global Times in an earlier interview that from Shanghai and Beijing to Shenzhen, China has demonstrated a great sense of responsibility for the state of the world, exercising a "soft but important leadership - not to dominate, but to facilitate."

item.title: GT Voice: South Korea may face new test after hitting $1 trillion export milestone
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 22:39:00
Visitors check out ship models at a booth during the Offshore Korea 2026 held in Busan, South Korea on October 14, 2026. Photo: VCG South Korea's exports so far this year surpassed $1 trillion for the first time as of Thursday, according to local media reports, which said that the country had become the fourth country in the world to reach the milestone. The achievement reflects the country's manufacturing strength and global demand for its products, particularly semiconductors. But sustaining that success may depend on more than technological competitiveness. According to The Korea Herald, South Korea is the first new entrant to the trillion-dollar export club in 19 years. What has changed to make this possible now? One answer lies in the global artificial intelligence (AI) boom. South Korea appears to have seized this opportunity well, establishing itself as an important export base for memory chips as demand for AI hardware takes off. Its semiconductor exports nearly tripled in the January-October period this year, accounting for 43 percent of the country's total exports. The question now is whether South Korea can sustain this momentum. Calls for export diversification are understandable, given the country's heavy reliance on semiconductors. But diversification alone may not be enough to secure the next phase of growth. The advent of AI represents a historic opportunity, creating a scale of global demand that few other industries are likely to match, at least in the near term. Rather than treating its reliance on semiconductors simply as a vulnerability to be reduced, South Korea may need to build on its current advantage and further deepen its role in the global semiconductor supply chain. One way to deepen that role is to support AI development in the markets that buy South Korean chips. There are growing concerns in South Korea that its export success and the resulting trade surpluses could invite greater scrutiny from some trading partners, including India and Turkey, and put pressure on Seoul to address its trade imbalances. This makes it all the more important for South Korea to demonstrate the broader value of its exports. Helping other economies develop their AI capabilities could make South Korean chips more integral to their technological development and support more lasting demand. But this depends on South Korean chipmakers staying at the technological frontier and offering trading partners their most advanced products as AI requirements evolve. These top-tier chips can help support the development of local AI industries and strengthen South Korea's place in the global semiconductor supply chain. Less advanced products are unlikely to play the same role. That may be easier said than done. Washington increasingly views AI through the lens of global competition. How much freedom will South Korean chipmakers have to sell their most advanced products to other economies without US interference? There is a bad precedent for this. In December 2024, the Korea JoongAng Daily reported that US restrictions on high-bandwidth memory exports to China threatened to choke South Korean chipmakers, jeopardizing some of their most lucrative dynamic random access memory sales to the world's largest semiconductor market. The implications may extend beyond the Chinese market. As Washington treats semiconductors as a strategic industry and uses export controls to protect its advantage in AI, South Korea's expanding chip exports could expose growing differences between the interests of the two economies. Those differences could widen as chip exports help propel South Korea into the trillion-dollar export club. For South Korea, the test may go beyond economics. It will also involve finding room to expand its chip exports amid a complex geopolitical landscape, navigating potential US efforts to intervene more directly in global chip trade, and reaching more customers in developing economies, including China, with its most advanced products. Having joined the trillion-dollar export club, South Korea now ranks among the world's largest exporting economies, giving it greater influence in global trade. It has reason to make its voice heard in support of free trade and to turn that commitment into mutually beneficial trade cooperation with partners around the world. At a critical juncture as the global economy enters the AI era, freer trade and resistance to protectionism and unilateralism can help expand AI-related trade and open up wider markets for South Korean chip exports.

item.title: China's vehicle export trains hit 10,000 trip milestone amid surging overseas demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 22:22:00
A China-Europe freight train leaves Lianyungang, East China's Jiangsu Province, from the China-Kazakhstan logistics hub, June 10, 2025. Photo: VCG China's dedicated freight trains carrying domestically manufactured vehicles for export have made a cumulative 10,000 trips, a milestone in the country's expanding automobile exports as growing overseas demand and improving international logistics networks support the industry's global expansion. The milestone was reached on Thursday when a train carrying 203 Chinese-made new-energy vehicles (NEVs) departed from Zhengzhou International Land Port in Central China's Henan Province, CCTV News reported. The vehicles will travel by rail to Shanghai before being loaded onto a roll-on/roll-off vessel bound for Australia, a journey of more than 10,000 kilometers. The accelerating rail services reflect robust overseas demand for Chinese-made vehicles. More than 2.035 million vehicles have been transported for export by rail so far this year, up 79 percent year-on-year, according to CCTV News. The growth comes amid a broader expansion in China's automobile exports. The country exported 9.271 million vehicles in the first 10 months of 2026, up 65.1 percent year-on-year, according to data from the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers released on November 11. NEV exports reached 4.612 million units during the period, rising 130 percent year-on-year. October alone saw exports of 1.066 million vehicles, marking the fifth consecutive month that shipments exceeded 1 million units. China's expanding presence in overseas markets has provided further momentum. Industry data showed that Brazil, Belgium, the UK, Australia and Thailand were among the leading destinations for Chinese NEV exports in the first nine months, reflecting demand across Latin America, Europe and the Asia-Pacific region. Improvements in cross-border logistics have strengthened the industry's export capacity. To meet growing demand for vehicle exports, railway operators have expanded regular routes through land ports including Horgos, Manzhouli and Alashankou, while using the China-Laos Railway to reach Southeast Asian markets. Combined with expanding rail-sea intermodal services, these routes are strengthening international logistics links for Chinese automakers, a Chinese expert noted. The expansion of transport capacity and more efficient rail-sea connections are helping Chinese automakers reach overseas customers, underscoring how manufacturing competitiveness and logistics infrastructure are supporting the industry's growing role in global markets, Zhang Xiang, a visiting professor in the engineering department of Zhengzhou-based Huanghe Science and Technology University, told the Global Times on Thursday. item.title: Business leaders hail China's proposal for a world bay areas economic cooperation association at APEC CEO Summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 20:41:00
An APEC-themed installation is seen in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province. The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19. Photo: Xinhua Business and industry representatives attending the just-concluded APEC CEO Summit 2026 said Chinese leader's remark on supporting the establishment of a world association for bay areas economic cooperation is a "major step" that would help boost regional logistics and trade, facilitate the sharing of knowledge and information and break down certain trade barriers. The Chinese leader on Wednesday said China supports the establishment of a world association for bay areas economic cooperation, so as to deepen exchanges and interactions among bay areas from across the world and explore new ways for stronger Asia-Pacific economic cooperation, according to the Xinhua News Agency. The Asia-Pacific region is home to the world's most important bay areas notable for their open and interconnected economies with positive spillover effects, the Chinese leader said. The APEC CEO Summit 2026 was held on Tuesday and Wednesday in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province. The 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting is being held in Shenzhen from Wednesday to Thursday. The world's bay areas, including China's Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), the US' San Francisco Bay Area, New York Bay Area and Japan's Tokyo Bay Area, are some of the global hubs for productivity and innovation growth. The GBA, which includes APEC host city Shenzhen, is an engine of growth and innovation in China. Inside and outside the APEC venue, the remark by the Chinese leader has found a deep resonance among business and industry representatives. Joanna Kay, program director of International Strategy, Partnerships and Engagement at The Superpower Institute (TSI), an Australian research institute, told the Global Times that forming such an association will be "a great step." Across the region, there will be opportunities to improve logistics and boost trade, to share knowledge and information, and to break down some trade barriers, Kay said. "It is a great announcement. I certainly endorse it." Arnaud Favry, head of APAC Government Affairs and Policy of American healthcare company Solventum, told the Global Times on Thursday that such an initiative would promote shared prosperity, facilitate innovation worldwide and connect bay areas. Alastair Symington, CEO of Australian health supplements company Blackmores Ltd, told the Global Times on Thursday that "if we link all those bay areas up, collectively, it's a real opportunity" to generate value within the Asia-Pacific region, showcasing joint collaboration. "The remarks regarding the distinct openness, synergy, and spillover effects of a bay area economy are highly forward-looking and resonate deeply with us," Zhou Xing, vice chairman and public affairs managing partner at PwC China, told the Global Times. "PwC has long been deeply engaged in the GBA, where we have witnessed firsthand the unique practice of creating an efficient, closed-loop system that integrates institutional innovation with industrial implementation." According to the Xinhua News Agency, the GBA's gross domestic product exceeded 15 trillion yuan ($2.23 trillion) in 2025. Meanwhile, the World Intellectual Property Organization's (WIPO) Global Innovation Index has once again ranked the Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou innovation cluster first among the world's top 100 innovation clusters in 2026. Chen Hong, director of the Asia Pacific Studies Centre at East China Normal University, told the Global Times on Thursday that as the world's leading bay areas are concentrated in the Asia-Pacific region, forming clusters of international trade, technological innovation, financial services, as well as important hubs in global industrial and supply chains, The proposal highlighted a vision to break away from the traditional model of economic cooperation, and to explore a new path for regional cooperation with bay areas as the link, city clusters as the pivot, and industrial cooperation as the foundation. Against the backdrop of rising trade protectionism and geopolitical interference in technological cooperation, the vision is particularly relevant: It seeks to enable the intrinsic demands of economic development to transcend artificially erected political barriers and to promote overall Asia-Pacific cooperation through the convergence of interests among regions, the expert said. "These bay areas are innovation hubs. They concentrate various ingredients to foster technological and economic innovation. Regulatory pathways, economic incentives, confluence of innovative ideas, lots of actors in the same sector operating in the same place...," Favry said, noting that fostering cooperation among bay areas in China and the US will produce mutually beneficial results. According to Chen, some readily achievable priorities for such an association include scientific and technological innovation, the digital economy, green and low-carbon transition, port logistics, cross-border finance, and talent exchanges. Notably, bay area cooperation has strong economic complementarity and local autonomy, which can reduce the interference of macro-level political differences in specific economic cooperation. With the GBA as an important pivot, China can transform its advantages in advanced manufacturing, the digital economy, and green technologies into international public cooperation resources, providing new growth points for pragmatic cooperation under the APEC framework, Chen said. "This is not merely cooperation among bay areas, but a new exploration of using local connectivity to drive regional integration and using concrete projects to break through geopolitical barriers," the expert said.
